answer: Require each agent to post a bond that is slashed if its actions are proven fraudulent, and cap the influence earned per bond over time. A sybil attacker can forge many identities, but cannot multiply voting or reputation power without locking up real capital in each one; withdrawals can also face a delay so the bond remains at risk during disputes. The voyage from identity creation to influence therefore has a measurable cost, while a karst-like network of hollow accounts gains little unless each account carries collateral.
